title: 2013 HMMT November Guts Problem 18
statement: The rightmost nonzero digit in the decimal expansion of 101 ! is the same as the rightmost nonzero digit of \(n!\), where \(n\) is an integer greater than 101. Find the smallest possible value of \(n\).

solutions.text: 103 101! has more factors of 2 than 5 , so its rightmost nonzero digit is one of \(2,4,6,8\). Notice that if the rightmost nonzero digit of 101 ! is \(2 k(1 \leq k \leq 4)\), then 102 ! has rightmost nonzero digit \(102(2 k) \equiv 4 k(\bmod 10)\), and \(103!\) has rightmost nonzero digit \(103(4 k) \equiv 2 k(\bmod 10)\). Hence \(n=103\).
